title: Persatrix Channel Configuration (v0.3.0+)
description: Internal-only schema until v1.0; `$id` may break across v0.x bumps without notice. Per RFC 0011 §A the canonical channel address is derived at runtime as `<channel_type>:<name>` (e.g., `group:planning`); the SQL `channels.id` PK column is a separate concern. DMs open on demand and are not declared here; threads anchor to a parent message and are likewise implicit.

max_channels.description: Global cap on declared named group channels. DMs and threads are not counted.

max_cascade_depth.description: Primary-enforcement cap on the cooperative-path cascade-depth backstop (RFC 0011 amendment 'Cascade-depth wire propagation', PR 2). Default is 5, aligned with the Python dispatcher's `max_cascade_depth` (agents/dispatch.py). The Go loader treats a zero or absent value as 'use the orchestrator default' so the backstop cannot be silently disabled from config (ChannelRouter.SetMaxCascadeDepth ignores non-positive overrides). Negative values are not permitted by the schema so an operator typo surfaces at `make validate` time rather than as a silent fall-back at startup.

default_interaction_budget_tokens.description: RFC 0030 Layer 1 (v0.3.8) fleet-wide per-interaction cost ceiling in tokens, applied to any channel that omits its own `interaction_budget_tokens`. Opt-in: 0 (the default) means uncapped, so the ceiling is additive and existing channels are unchanged. Once an interaction's running token total would cross the resolved ceiling, the wallet denies further leases in that interaction (`INTERACTION_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, fail-closed — the LLM call does not happen). Negative is rejected at load time.

default_max_replies_per_participant.description: RFC 0030 Layer 2 (v0.3.8) fleet-wide per-participant reply budget, applied to any channel that omits its own `max_replies_per_participant_per_interaction`. Opt-in: 0 (the default) means uncapped, so fair-turn-taking is additive and existing channels are unchanged. With K>0, a participant's (K+1)th publish in one interaction is rejected pre-persistence (HTTP 429); a human principal listed in `governance.exempt_principals` is exempt. Negative is rejected at load time.

default_interaction_idle_timeout_seconds.description: Fleet-wide interaction idle window in seconds (the RFC 0030 interaction-id producer, IP3), applied to any channel that omits its own `interaction_idle_timeout_seconds`: a publish arriving more than this long after the channel's last one retires the open interaction and mints a fresh one (`interaction_closed{trigger=idle}`). Absent means 600 — RFC 0020 §B's idle default, matching the agent-side `interaction_idle_timeout_sec` so governance and memory boundaries roughly coincide. An explicit 0 disables idle rotation fleet-wide (distinct from absent). Thread channels ignore the resolved value entirely — a thread IS its interaction. Negative is rejected at load time.

governance.description: RFC 0030 (v0.3.8) fleet-wide governance settings that are not per-channel.

exempt_principals.description: Principal classes exempt from the Layer 2 per-participant reply budget (§OQ-7). The only recognised value is `human`, which maps to the `user` participant type on the wire so a human driving a conversation is never throttled by the budget meant to keep agents from dominating. An entry with no mapping is ignored (fails open to 'not exempt').

floor_control.description: RFC 0030 Layer 2.5 speaker serialization (floor control): candidate responders take the floor one at a time, each reading the prior speaker's reply, instead of replying concurrently and mutually-blind. As of v0.3.6 the resolved default is ON for every declared (group) channel — omit the key to inherit it; set it false to opt a channel back out. Below two responders (e.g. a DM) it is a no-op regardless. The per-turn wait is floor_turn_timeout_seconds.

floor_turn_timeout_seconds.description: Per-speaker turn timeout for floor control (RFC 0030 amendment decision D2): how long the serialized loop waits for one speaker's reply before advancing to the next responder. Distinct from the 5s per-recipient fanout timeout — a floor turn is LLM-latency-bound. Absent uses the 45s default; the Go loader treats a zero/absent value as 'use the default' and rejects negatives at load time.

salience_max_channel_members.description: RFC 0030 Tier B (v0.3.8) channel-size cap (TB6 / amendment OQ #4): above this many candidate responders, the agent-side salience bid is skipped entirely and open-floor `participant`/`chair` members fall back to `addressed`-only, keeping a cheap bid × N members bounded on a large channel. Absent uses the 20 default (kept in lock-step with the agent-side DEFAULT_SALIENCE_MAX_CHANNEL_MEMBERS); the Go loader treats a zero/absent value as 'use the default' and rejects negatives at load time. The resolved value is carried to the agent on the ChannelMessageEvent wire.

interaction_budget_tokens.description: RFC 0030 Layer 1 (v0.3.8) per-interaction cost ceiling in tokens for this channel. Once an interaction on this channel would cross the ceiling, the wallet denies further leases (`INTERACTION_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, fail-closed). Opt-in: absent or 0 inherits `default_interaction_budget_tokens` (itself 0 = uncapped) — unlike `salience_max_channel_members`, 0 is NOT normalized to a non-zero default, because uncapped is a meaningful value. Negative is rejected at load time. The channel-over-fleet precedence is resolved at read time.

max_replies_per_participant_per_interact.description: RFC 0030 Layer 2 (v0.3.8) per-participant reply budget for this channel: a participant's (K+1)th publish in one interaction on this channel is rejected pre-persistence (HTTP 429 + `ErrParticipantBudgetExhausted`), so the dropped message never enters channel history. Opt-in: absent or 0 inherits `default_max_replies_per_participant` (itself 0 = uncapped) — like `interaction_budget_tokens`, 0 is NOT normalized to a non-zero default, because uncapped is a meaningful value. A human principal in `governance.exempt_principals` is exempt. Negative is rejected at load time. The channel-over-fleet precedence is resolved at read time.

end_vote_threshold.description: RFC 0030 Layer 4 (v0.3.8) end-of-interaction quorum (K) for this channel: when K distinct participants emit an `END_INTERACTION_VOTE` action within `end_vote_window` consecutive turns, the interaction closes on its own and the orchestrator stops fanning out new replies (§H). Absent uses the K=2 default (one agent saying 'done' is not consensus; two distinct agents in close succession is); the Go loader treats a zero/absent value as 'use the default' — unlike `interaction_budget_tokens`, 0 is NOT a meaningful 'uncapped' value here — and rejects negatives at load time. Still opt-in: with no agent emitting the vote action, a populated K never fires, so existing channels are unchanged.

end_vote_window.description: RFC 0030 Layer 4 (v0.3.8) end-of-interaction recency window (W) for this channel: an end-vote counts toward the `end_vote_threshold` quorum only while it is within W consecutive turns of the current turn, so a stale vote from much earlier no longer counts ('votes must be recent'). A 'turn' is any tracked publish in the interaction (every message, not only votes), so in a busy channel the K distinct votes must land within W publishes of each other — tune W up if intervening chatter is starving the quorum. Absent uses the W=3 default (wide enough to survive an intervening one-off comment); the Go loader treats a zero/absent value as 'use the default' and rejects negatives at load time.

escalation_chair_id.description: The chair-stall-escalation amendment (RFC 0030 minimal Layer 5 slice, v0.3.8): the member who receives ONE forced turn after a stalled floor round (zero replies across ≥1 granted turns on the channel's open interaction) — prompted to synthesize and cast its end-of-discussion vote, or to call on the member best placed to continue. Must be one of this channel's declared members (the loader rejects a non-member loudly); it need not be declared `chair`. Closing still requires the Layer 4 vote quorum — the chair proposes, the quorum disposes. Absent (the default) disables escalation; deliberately distinct from the v0.4.0 moderator's `moderator_agent_id` (a non-participant trusted closer).

interaction_idle_timeout_seconds.description: This channel's interaction idle window in seconds (the RFC 0030 interaction-id producer, IP3): a publish arriving more than this long after the channel's last one retires the open interaction and mints a fresh one. Tri-state, unlike the integer knobs above: absent inherits `default_interaction_idle_timeout_seconds` (itself defaulting to 600), while an explicit 0 disables idle rotation for this channel — so no `default` is declared here (a schema default would erase the absent-vs-0 distinction the loader's pointer field preserves). Negative is rejected at load time.

members.description: Explicit, auditable membership list. The v0.2-era `members: "all"` shorthand was dropped per RFC 0011.

respond.description: Member disposition (RFC 0030 relevance amendment). Recommended vocabulary: `participant` (joins the open floor — speaks on un-addressed messages, subject to the Tier B salience bid), `chair` (a low-threshold facilitator: a `participant` that clears the salience bid readily and keeps the discussion moving — v0.3.8; it CANNOT close an interaction, convergence is owned by the governance layers, and its Layer 5 moderator hooks are reserved/inert until v0.4.0), `addressed` (speaks only when @-mentioned or replied to), `observer` (never speaks). The legacy values `always`/`when_mentioned`/`never` keep working and map to `participant`/`addressed`/`observer` respectively; the Go loader normalizes the disposition vocabulary back to the legacy three at load time (`chair` → `always` + a low default `threshold`), so the wire `respond_policy` and every downstream reader are unchanged.

threshold.description: Per-disposition salience threshold for the v0.3.8 Tier B relevance bid: an open-floor `participant` only reaches the (expensive) quality turn when its cheap salience bid clears this bar. Only meaningful on an open-floor disposition (`participant`/`chair`/legacy `always`); the Go loader rejects a `threshold` set on `addressed`/`observer`/`when_mentioned`, where no bid runs — a cross-field rule JSON Schema cannot express, so a schema-valid config can still fail to load. Bias-to-silence — an absent/unset threshold biases toward NOT replying on ambiguous open-floor traffic (the conservative default; calibration is post-soak). `chair` members get a low default so they speak readily. Bounded to the `[0, 1]` salience range (salience is clipped to `[0.0, 1.0]` per RFC 0024; mirrors `autonomy.salience_threshold` in agent.schema.json).

messageMetadata.description: Optional metadata bag on the publish payload (POST /api/v1/channels/{id}/messages → publishMessageRequest.metadata). Carries cross-cutting wire-level fields that are not part of the core message body. Documented here rather than in the channels.yaml config schema because the config file has no metadata of its own — this definition pins the REST publish contract, mirrored on the gRPC side by typed fields on ChannelMessageEvent.

cascade_depth.description: Hop count along the cooperative-path cascade chain (RFC 0011 amendment 'Cascade-depth wire propagation'). Documented operational range is [0, max_cascade_depth] (default cap 5). The schema enforces a lower bound only — values above the cap are accepted and clamped server-side at the orchestrator's publish boundary so a publisher does not need to know the deployment's current cap to compose a payload. Mirrors the typed `int32 cascade_depth = 11` field on `ChannelMessageEvent` (proto/task.proto).

interaction_id.description: RFC 0020 interaction_id of the open Interaction this message belongs to (RFC 0030 deterministic governance layers, v0.3.8). Opaque string token — RFC 0020 §D names it a ULID, but the agent-side implementation mints a uuid4 (agents/memory/interactions.py), so do not assume ULID sortability. Optional: absent is the untracked / pre-v0.3.8 case, which leaves every governance layer (Layer 1 cost ceiling, Layer 2 reply budget, Layer 4 end-of-interaction votes) at its uncapped default, so the field is additive. When a publisher supplies this key the orchestrator lifts it onto the typed `string interaction_id = 17` field on `ChannelMessageEvent` (proto/task.proto) so the value survives the publish→fanout boundary that has no metadata map. Bounded at 128 (mirrors the agent receive path's thread_id cap, generous over the 36-char uuid4) — the layer PRs key per-interaction maps on this value, so an over-length claim is treated as untracked (the value dropped) rather than riding an unbounded map key through. This schema is the documentary expression of that bound (`maxLength` counts code units); the runtime enforcement counts UTF-8 bytes and lives at BOTH boundaries that touch the value — the orchestrator publish boundary (`readInteractionID`, internal/channels/interaction_id.go) and the agent receive seed (`seed_wire_metadata`, agents/channel_wire_metadata.py), each degrading to untracked rather than failing the dispatch. The producer is live since v0.3.8 (the interaction-id producer plan): the orchestrator's own resolver stamps the key on every routed publish (`publishCommit`, internal/channels/router_publish_async.go), REPLACING any inbound claim — a publisher-supplied value is read only for the divergence debug log and never keys governance state.

end_interaction_vote.description: RFC 0030 Layer 4 (v0.3.8) end-of-interaction vote flag: when an agent emits an `END_INTERACTION_VOTE` action, the publish that carries it sets this to `true` so the orchestrator counts it toward the channel's `end_vote_threshold` quorum (scoped by `interaction_id`; a vote with no `interaction_id` is ignored). Absent/false is an ordinary message. The orchestrator reads it at the publish boundary (`readEndInteractionVote`, internal/channels/end_vote.go) and, once K distinct participants have voted within `end_vote_window` consecutive turns, closes the interaction and suppresses further fanout. The producer is live since v0.3.8: the Python vote producer (`publish_end_interaction_vote`, agents/end_vote_action.py) merges the flag into every published vote's metadata.

previous_interaction_id.description: RFC 0030 producer plan OQ 5 (v0.3.8): the channel's most recently RETIRED interaction id, stamped by the orchestrator (`publishCommit`, internal/channels/router_publish_async.go) onto every publish of the SUCCESSOR interaction together with `previous_interaction_close_trigger` — the close-cause attribution the agent-side rotation close uses to label the local boundary truthfully. Router-authoritative like `interaction_id`: an inbound claim under this key is STRIPPED on commit (a publisher can never forge a close cause), so on read surfaces the value is always the resolver's own record. Absent is the no-retiree case (fresh channel, post-restart re-mint, pre-v0.3.8 rows) and receivers keep the legacy structural label. Same 128-byte bound and enforcement posture as `interaction_id`; the pair is validated as a unit at both the dispatcher lift (`readPreviousClose`, internal/channels/interaction_id.go) and the agent receive seed (`seed_wire_metadata`, agents/channel_wire_metadata.py) — mirrored on the gRPC side by the typed `string previous_interaction_id = 20` field on `ChannelMessageEvent` (proto/task.proto).

previous_interaction_close_trigger.description: The trigger that retired `previous_interaction_id` — `idle` (lazy idle rotation) or `end_votes` (Layer 4 quorum close), the §L instrument vocabulary. Set iff `previous_interaction_id` is set (the pair travels and validates as a unit; a lone trigger attributes nothing). Stamped and stripped exactly like its sibling; the agent-side rotation close maps `idle` → the `idle_gap` close reason and everything else (including absent) → the legacy `structural` label, so an unrecognised value degrades rather than failing the dispatch. Mirrors the typed `string previous_interaction_close_trigger = 21` field on `ChannelMessageEvent` (proto/task.proto).
